uncited: It builds on [Ray Marching Dither](3269-ray-marching-dither.md) by applying perturbation to the step size rather than just UV coordinates.
- No specific complex data structures are required.
A hash function is needed to generate a deterministic random value per pixel/ray.
Calculate a jitter offset based on the texture coordinate and dithering strength.
Determine the start time for the ray march by adding the jitter offset to the minimum distance.

Ray Marching Jittering is a technique to reduce aliasing artifacts, specifically banding, in volume rendering by introducing random variation to the ray marching step size [S2, unofficial].

The claim states that Ray Marching Jittering reduces aliasing artifacts (specifically banding) by introducing random variation to the step size. Source [S2] explicitly confirms that fixed step sizes introduce aliasing in the form of 'clearly defined bands of intensity' and that jittering (adding random variation to the step size, specifically between 0.5x and 1.5x the fixed step size) effectively removes this banding.
